games.name: Maneater
games.summary: Unreal Engine 4.25, Direct3D 11, Denuvo Anti-Tamper. Hangs on the spinning-shark loading screen under FEX with stock settings.
notes: Denuvo is the most likely cause of the endless spinning-shark screen: it uses self-modifying code, and FEX's faster presets skip the checks that catch it. This profile turns full code checks on and hides the hypervisor bit, as DroidDeck's own Denuvo preset does, but keeps main TSO on so UE4's loading threads don't deadlock.
OPENSSL_ia32cap=:~0x20000000 hides the CPU's SHA extensions from the game's old bundled OpenSSL. That is the Steam community fix for Maneater freezing or crashing at startup on newer CPUs.

The intro logo movies are renamed so the game doesn't have to play video through Media Foundation at boot, and Engine.ini turns off motion blur, depth of field, chromatic aberration and lens flares and lowers volumetric fog. Revert undoes all of it.
Be online for the first launch after applying. Denuvo has to re-activate, and ProtonDB users report the game freezing at startup when offline.
The first launch can sit on the loading screen for several minutes while FEX translates code and DXVK builds shaders. Give it 5 to 10 minutes before you call it a hang.
Denuvo can lock the game for 24 hours after about 5 hardware changes. Avoid switching Proton versions or FEX presets for this game repeatedly.

tweaks.name: Skip intro movies
tweaks.description: Renames the logo MP4s in Maneater/Content/Movies, so the game does not have to play video through Media Foundation at boot. They are renamed, not deleted, and revert puts them back.

tweaks.name: Handheld performance tweaks (Engine.ini)
tweaks.description: Turns off motion blur, depth of field, chromatic aberration and lens flares, and lowers volumetric fog. That is cheaper on the Adreno 740 and makes fewer shaders to build on first load.

profile.name: Best compatibility + performance
profile.description: Full self-modifying-code checks and a hidden hypervisor bit for Denuvo, with main TSO on so UE4's threads don't deadlock. Vector and memcpy TSO stay off and multiblock stays on for speed.
